findings.reason: the section requires a recorded conflict and an immediate retry-after-promotion at once, which the existing pass cannot both give, so either the done-when's timing or the design (exempt the queued-behind overlap from the retry back-off) must change before a node builds it.
findings.text: while the earlier run is still working, §18 has the later request's launch "refused on that claim" and "put back in the queue with the conflict recorded as its last failure"; a recorded non-lane-hold failure starts the admission back-off (`_retry_backoff_hold` in `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:337` holds until `retry_at`, set by `_stamp_failure` at line 390 to `now + 30s·2ⁿ` capped at 600s, and a `ScopeConflict` is not a `LaneHeld`/`LanePaused` hold per `_is_lane_hold` at line 234), so when the earlier run is promoted the later one is still held by its own back-off and cannot launch "on the next pass" — the done-when as written is unreachable on the real pass loop, and the builder will either weaken the assertion (hiding the behaviour) or bend the pass to defeat the back-off
